title.ko: 저널리즘 문체: headline · lede · inverted pyramid · sources said · is set to · slams
title.en: journalistic style: headline, lede, inverted pyramid, sources said, is set to, slams

explain.ko: 신문 기사는 가장 중요한 정보를 먼저 쓰는 역피라미드(inverted pyramid) 구조를 따릅니다. 헤드라인(headline)은 짧은 단어와 현재 시제를 즐겨 쓰고(Opposition slams policy), 리드(lede)는 누가, 무엇을, 언제, 어디서를 한 문장에 담습니다. is set to ..., sources said 같은 표현이 자주 쓰입니다. 좋은 기자는 출처를 밝히고 사실과 의견을 구분하며 사건을 과장하지 않습니다.
explain.en: News articles follow the inverted pyramid, putting the most important information first. Headlines favour short words and the present tense (Opposition slams policy), and the lede packs who, what, when and where into one sentence. Expressions such as is set to ... and sources said are frequent. A good reporter names sources, separates fact from opinion and does not sensationalise.

items.passage:
JOURNALISM LECTURE
Writing a good article
An article follows the inverted pyramid, putting the most important information first. Write headlines short and strong, and ledes to contain who, what, when and where. Naming sources and separating fact from opinion are the basis of trust.

trans.ko:
